description:
The rare-event estimator built to its preregistered design, with unbiasedness and interval coverage demonstrated against exactly known cases.

## Background

A rare-event estimator's output cannot be checked by looking at it: the events it estimates are ones direct sampling never observes. Its credibility comes entirely from behaving correctly where the answer is known. At $k = 1$ the deficiency probability is exactly $q^{-n}$ at every $n$, and small $(q, n, k)$ are exhaustively enumerable, which gives a ladder of cases with known answers running from trivially small up to the edge of what direct sampling can reach.

Coverage is a separate property from unbiasedness and is demonstrated separately: an estimator can be unbiased while reporting intervals that contain the true value far less often than their nominal level claims, and it is the interval that a reader of the result will rely on.

## Success Criteria

- [aspirational] REQ-01: The estimator implements the preregistered proposal and weighting, and a test asserts the implemented weights match the specification on hand-checked cases.
- [aspirational] REQ-02: Unbiasedness is demonstrated against cases whose probability is known exactly, with the estimator's mean over repeated independent runs agreeing with the exact value within its own interval.
- [aspirational] REQ-03: Interval coverage is demonstrated empirically: over repeated runs at a stated nominal level, the fraction of intervals containing the exact value matches the nominal level within its own binomial interval.
- [aspirational] REQ-04: A deviation from the preregistered design made during implementation is recorded with its reason, and the validation is judged against the design as amended rather than silently against the new behaviour.
- [aspirational] REQ-05: Draws come from the reserved rare-event stream purpose, so no such draw can enter a published zero-fraction cell.
- [aspirational] REQ-06: A configuration whose effective sample size falls below the design's usability threshold is reported as unusable rather than as an estimate.

## Notes

Every criterion here is aspirational. A demonstrated failure to achieve coverage is a recorded result and closes this work honestly; it is not a reason to relax the criterion.

The estimate at the preregistered beyond-reach target is separate work behind this leaf on a dependency edge, producing its own receipted artefact.
title: Rare-event estimator with demonstrated unbiasedness and coverage
